summary: The web workspace opened the roster EventSource on mount and also force-reopened it on the initial CONNECTED transition of its separate workspace WebSocket. A connection gate now suppresses only that redundant initial reopen while preserving a forced refresh after a later WebSocket recovery. The roster manager's start() is also idempotent, while explicit reconnect() still replaces the stream. The server's documented 10-second SSE response lifetime remains intentional and causes sequential browser EventSource requests.

checks.name: Test-first regression before implementation
checks.observation: The initial-connect regression failed because the gate did not yet exist; after that fix, the repeated-start regression failed because start() opened a second EventSource. Both failures were expected before their respective fixes.

checks.name: Focused roster event stream tests
checks.observation: Roster stream lifecycle and workspace realtime tests pass, including suppressing the initial reconnect, refreshing when the workspace mounts with an already-connected socket, and keeping start() idempotent while explicit reconnect() replaces the stream.

checks.name: TypeScript check and production frontend build
checks.observation: vue-tsc and Vite production build pass. Vite reports the existing LiveKit chunk-size advisory (>500 kB).

checks.name: Live browser connection count and reconnect cadence
checks.command: Inspect browser Network panel for /api/v1/voice/rosters/events during initial load and across one 10-second response close.
checks.observation: No browser tab is available and the Mac is locked.

remaining: Verify in a live browser that initial workspace load creates no extra manual EventSource reopen, that the expected sequential reconnect follows the server's 10-second response close, and that a later workspace WebSocket recovery refreshes the roster.
